controls: control.replay.v1 on every arm (weather is seeded: BIT replay must hold)

decision_criteria.NEW_PHENOMENON: all gates pass and erase < sham (retention load-bearing; the gates e07 refused, P1/P4, pass in BEE)
decision_criteria.PHENOMENON_ABSENT: gates pass but erase ~= sham ~= STATIC (weather has no effect: retention not load-bearing)
decision_criteria.PHENOMENON_PRESERVED: a gate refuses as in e07 (BEE is also inconclusive for the same structural reason)

gates.P1_damage_fires: erase ws_damage > 0 AND erase mean charge < STATIC mean charge on the panel
gates.P3_changes_behaviour: erase mean charge != STATIC mean charge
gates.P4_separable: erase mean charge != sham mean charge, and sham ~= STATIC (sham loses no information)

prereg.initial_state: each organism starts each episode with an empty workspace; state accrues across ticks

entries.reason: the three arms map one-to-one onto the weather substrate's modes

entries.bee: kv_weather erase: delete the workspace value when weather fires
entries.reason: BEE damages the organism's WORKSPACE (a substrate door it owns), the state it can lose
entries.source: weather erases an organism's retained state

entries.bee: kv_weather sham: rewrite the same value, pay the write, ws_damage counts equally
entries.reason: the sham fires exactly as often (same ws_damage) and pays a write, but the value is unchanged
entries.source: SHAMWEATHER pays the same cost, loses no information

entries.bee: statemachine.v2, write_every=1 (writes its workspace every tick)
entries.reason: a finite-state controller with a workspace it reads and writes; a memory user by construction
performance is the resource the organism ends with

entries.bee: P1 damage fires / P2 uses state / P3 changes behaviour / P4 WEATHER separable from SHAMWEATHER / P5 deterministic
entries.reason: the same five predicates, evaluated on BEE's accounting, objectives and replay
BEE can damage the WORKSPACE (a declared door) but not a statemachine's internal `state` register; only externalised, retained state is in reach of a substrate
entries.source: damage to state the organism does not expose

entries.reason: BEE authors no scientific conclusion; the comparison packet is the conclusion layer

prereg.question: Does erasing a memory-using organism's retained workspace (WEATHER) reduce its final charge beyond a cost-matched sham that rewrites the same value (SHAMWEATHER)? I.e. is retained state load-bearing, and is WEATHER separable from SHAMWEATHER?
prereg.stopping_rules: fixed panel and budget; a gate that fails REFUSES the reading (as e07 did), it is not forced
